segments.text: Good afternoon. This is Akash Vani and I am Valsa Williams with the Midday News.
The headlines Defense Minister Rajnath Singh lashes out at Congress over protests in Delhi,
accuses it of seeking regime change through violence and anarchy after facing electoral defeat.
India emerges as key source of private capital mobilized by World Bank Group.
Government raises petrol export duty to Rs 2.5 per litre, cuts diesel levy to Rs 8.5 per
litre.
Air India cancels flights to and from Riyadh, Damam and Jalta until 20th October amid evolving
situation in Saudi Arabia and in Women's Cricket India to face Zimbabwe in first T20
International of Three Mad series in Raipur this evening.
The Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today raised questions about the intention of the Congress
party regarding the recent protests and said the party is misguiding people by giving wrong
information and wants to take revenge for their defeat in elections by resorting to
violence and anarchy.
Addressing media in Lucknow, Mr Singh attacked sharply on the Congress party and its leader
Rahul Gandhi by saying they should not use the title of Gandhi as the father
of the nation suspended his movement after the Chaudhary Chaudhary violence and the
Congress party and their associate organizations are openly saying they want to topple the government
and want regime change for which they are taking inspiration from Bangladesh.
India's reputation is increasing in the international community,
where there used to be a defense production of 40,000 crores.
Today, there is a defense production of more than 180,000 crores.
regime change and resistance and the word that comes out of the road, not the parliament,
has become clear today.
Whatever is happening in Delhi is not through constitutional arrangements, but through imperialism,
is a condemnable attempt to derail India's progress.
India has emerged alongside the United States and Britain as a leading source of private
capital mobilized by the World Bank Group.
World Bank President Ajay Banga highlighted India's growing role in international development
financing during his address to the World Bank annual meeting plenary in Bangkok.
He stated that last year, capital was mobilized from investors in 110 countries, with the
United States, Britain and India leading the way.
Last year, the capital we mobilized was from investors in 110 countries.
The U.S., the U.K., India led the way.
But guess what? Investors came from Romania and Chile and Poland and Brazil.
More countries are attracting investment, more are supplying it.
Across it all, nearly 55% of our financing and the private capital we mobilized went to
the five sectors we care about – infrastructure and energy,
agribusiness, health, tourism and value-added manufacturing.
These sectors are the ones that raise productivity and create locally relevant jobs
in those economies in the developing world.
The Government has raised the export duty on petrol to 2.5 rupees per litre from 50
pesos, while the export duty on diesel has been reduced from 16 rupees to 8.5 rupees
per litre. According to a notification issued by the Finance Ministry, the revised rates
have come into effect from today. The rate of duty on exports of ATF continues to
remain at 10.5 rupees per litre. There is no change in the existing exercise duty
rates on petrol and diesel cleared for domestic consumption. The rates are prescribed based
on the average international prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF prevailing during
the period since the last review. The rates are being revised on a fortnightly basis,
and the last such revision was undertaken on the first of this month.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah has reiterated that when the BJP government assumes power
in Punjab. It will work with full commitment to make the state safe and free from drugs
and gangsters. In a social media post, Mr. Shah said, the aim is to dismantle the drug
trade, secure the future of the youth, and take stern action against criminals and establish
a rule of law where no citizen is forced to live under the shadow of fear.
Vice-presidency Biradakrishnan today commissioned the indigenously built multi-purpose vessel
INS Samarthak into the Indian Navy at INS Kadam Naval Base in Karwar, Karnataka.
Chief of the naval staff, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, senior naval officials, and Karnataka
Labour Minister Santosh Ladd attended the ceremony.
In a statement, the vice president said INS Samarthak is the first of four such
vessels being constructed indigenously, with over 75% indigenous content.
With more than 75% indigenous content, Samarthak demonstrates the self-reliance, independence
is no longer merely an aspiration but a reality.
I firmly believe that indigenous content is much more than a percentage on paper.
Behind every homegrown component is the contribution of Indian designer, engineer, technician,
manufacturing, MSME, startup or research institution.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of service to the nation through public service and an unwavering commitment
to the country.
Inspired by this vision of service and good governance, the government is continuously
working towards achieving the goal of a developed India by 2047.
In today's special series, we bring you a report on how a far-reaching initiative like
Aik Bharat Shreist Bharat is translating this vision into reality by connecting the country's
linguistic and cultural diversity.
The Aik Bharat Shreist Bharat initiative, launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, aims
to promote mutual understanding and strength and ties among people from different states.
The Prime Minister has repeatedly emphasised that every Indian language and culture is
the source of national pride. In the Kolhans region, West Singhum district reflects a rich
linguistic and cultural diversity that is integral to local life. In Kolhans, a prominent
tribal language Ho embodies the region's unique culture and identity. To explore and
understand this linguistic and cultural richness, students from Odisha, West Bengal and other parts
of the country regularly visit educational institutions in the region. The 400-old Royal
Palace of Sarai Kela Kharsama and its world-renowned Chow Dance tradition are also important
centres of cultural diversity. Despite differences in language, communication continues uninterrupted
with visitors learning local dialects and local residents learning languages spoken by the visitors.
Speaking about this linguistic exchange, Tarum Kumar Singh, a teacher from Sarai Kela, says
that language fosters mutual respect and strengthens the feeling of belonging to the entire country.
Sarai Kela district is not limited merely to chow dance and four card. Rather, it is home
to people from diverse communities, each with their own distinct attire, language,
cujin and traditions. They exemplify an unbreakable spirit of brotherhood, thereby strengthening
the foundation upon which the vision of Eik Bharat Sresht Bharat is built.
From Kul Haan to different parts of the country, languages and dialects may differ, but the
spirit of unity remains the same. With the lip energy from Chai Basa and Golag Bihari
from Saraykelakhar Sabha, Mahavish Rahman, Akashwani News, Rachi.
Welcome back to the midday news.
The Press Council of India, PCI, has issued guidelines for journalists covering protests
and demonstrations. The guidelines have been issued in view of the prevailing scenario and
the need to facilitate the orderly and effective coverage of protests and demonstrations. Under
the guidelines, journalists have been advised to carry identity cards issued by their media
organizations or press information bureau or PIB and directed at information and publicity
accreditation as applicable and keep them visibly displayed while covering demonstrations.
We have more from our correspondent.
The Press Council of India has advised media persons to maintain a reasonable and safe distance
from confrontations, particularly when tensions escalate or police action is anticipated.
The Council has asked the journalists to maintain neutrality and professionalism and
not to participate in demonstrations or interfere with protesters, counter protesters or police.
It urged journalists to be alert to changes in crowd behaviour and identify escape routes
in advance.
The guidelines stated that journalists should report events accurately, objectively, and
impartially.
They have been advised to distinguish verified facts from allegations, opinions, and unconfirmed
claims and follow the applicable norms of journalistic conduct on accuracy and fairness.
The council further suggested to verify information through multiple sources wherever
possible.
PCI has asked journalists not to broadcast or publish real-time police positions, tactical
movements or escape routes, as doing so can compromise safety or operational security.
With Anand Kumar, Shivamisha Akashpani, News, Delhi.
In view of a proposed protest today, Delhi Traffic Police has issued an advisory that
mentions traffic movement on certain roads in and around Karnat place is likely to
be affected from 3 p.m. today. Sharing an advisory, the traffic police directed
commuters to plan their journeys accordingly in advance. It advised using public transport
wherever possible, complying with the traffic personnel directions.
The traffic police also suggested people to stay updated
and follow their social media handle,
as traffic diversions may be implemented
depending on the prevailing situation.
In view of the evolving situation in Saudi Arabia,
Air India has cancelled its flights
to and from Riyadh, Damam and Jeddah
until the 20th of this month.
In a social media post, Air India said
said it is closely monitoring the developments and continuously assessing the situation to
ensure the safe resumption of its operations, its said passengers affected by these cancellations
are being offered a full refund.
The joint India-Russia military exercise INDRA 2026 is currently underway in Russia, featuring
coordinated naval, land and air operations.
The naval component has begun its harbour phase in Vladivostok.
The practical maritime phase will be held in the Sea of Japan on October 16 and 17.
Participating warships will carry out tactical maneuvers, artillery firing drills against
sea and aerial targets, inspection operations and rehearsals to liberate a vessel simulated
to have been seized by terrorists.
The higher reaches of Kashmir and Jammu regions, including Pir Ki Gali in Ponsh Sintan
and top in Kishtwar and Chattar Galla in Badarwa.
Received the season's first snowfall yesterday, while a sharp fall in the temperature has
been experienced in the plain areas of the region, a report.
There was heavy rain, hailstorm and windstorm in parts of the frontier district punch,
including Mander and Sorencourt late last evening.
Due to hailstorm, the crops were badly affected while power supply in many areas
of the district also remained hit.
The mountainous areas of Rajoridistic including Bhudal, Kotranka and Dharal beside Gulabgarh
and Mohor in Riyasi district also received snowfall.
However, the roads were operational.
Reports from Dodar, Ramban and Kishtwar said that Shiojdhar and other higher reaches
also received moderate to heavy snowfall of the October month last night.
With the heavy snowfall, Senthantop pass on Kishtwar, Kukarnag, Anantnag highway was blocked.
Padri Top on Badarwa Chamba Road was also blocked due to heavy snowfall and the road was closed.
Chhatragala Pass on Badarwa Bani Basodi, Patan Court Highway and Gul Danda Tourist Resort also
received fresh snowfall. This is Anne Gulsandaina for Akashwani News from Jammu.
Meanwhile, the Intermetrological Department has issued an orange-colour warning for heavy to
very heavy rainfall over south interior Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Buddhucherry and Karayaka.
today. The weather agency has forecast heavy rainfall over Andhra Pradesh, coastal Karnataka,
Kerala and Mahi till Monday. In women's cricket in double-phase Zimbabwe in the first T20 international
of the three-matte series in Raipur today, the match will begin at 7 p.m. IST. Benchmark
domestic equity indices were trading over half a percent up. In the afternoon session today,
the Sensex gained 385 points to 74,701, while the Nifty climbed 137 points to 23,135 when
reports last came in.
And now, before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh lashes out at Congress over protests in Delhi, accuses
it of seeking regime change through violence and anarchy, after facing electoral defeat.
India emerges as key source of private capital mobilized by World Bank Group.
Government raises petrol-expert-export-duty to Rs.2.5 per litre, cuts diesel-levy to Rs.8.5
per litre.
Air India cancels flights to and from Riyadh, Dhammam and Jaddah until 20 October amid evolving
situation in Saudi Arabia.
And in Women's Cricket, Inder to face Zimbabwe in 1st D-20 International of 3 Math series
in Raipur this evening.
With that, we end the midday news.
